correctness.rationale: On the tree K=Σ_i c_i/g_i, c_i=i(n-i), and Cauchy–Schwarz gives unique g_i=sqrt(c_i)/S_n. The rank-one Laplacian inverse formula identifies the marginal chord gain as the squared pair-voltage sum. Counting unordered injections crossing both path edges produces overlap min(i,j)(n-max(i,j)), yielding S_n²Theta; KKT residual S_n²(t-Theta) and strict convexity imply a unique optimizer and exact inactive equality case. Bounded kernel Riemann convergence gives F, and x=sin²u gives the checked elementary primitive with F(0,1)=pi²/4-2. For length ℓ=o(n), p/ℓ->kappa, the kernel converges in a bounded boundary layer to sqrt((kappa+min(u,v))/(kappa+max(u,v))); integration yields Phi(kappa), strictly increasing from 2/3 to 1. Independent exact small-rational identity and high-precision integral checks complement but do not replace proof.
residual_risks: Strict convexity holds on the connected domain with distinct simple-edge Laplacian directions; disconnected boundary is excluded by infinite K.

evidence: Earlier convex network allocation theorem applies abstractly to path plus chord; its path tree optimum is g_i∝sqrt(i(n-i)).
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general convex/KKT framework subsumes the finite activation mechanism; inspected sources do not themselves state the explicit continuum/mesoscopic critical-price results. The later budget augmentation paper remains a full-text reading risk.

In the inspected relevant path-design passages, no explicit scaled chord-price geometry F(a,b), Phi(kappa) or 2/3 boundary discount was found. Adjacent edge-addition literature uses fixed conductances or different budgets; a 2026 related abstract cannot rule out undisclosed equivalent formulas. The continuum position law and endpoint-to-interior 2/3→1 transition provide a previously implicit geometrical design threshold across scales. Exact KKT alone is not claimed new; natural asymptotic edge-regime analysis makes the added fact useful.
residual_risks: Not an optimization theorem for many shortcuts or nonlinear edge costs.
